title: Simulating the Evolution of Aging
beats: Dying seems bad; why doesn't natural selection extend lifespans? Baseline sim first, then aging models.
Patreon and sponsorship discussion, new tiers.
Mango forest, blobs eat, spend energy, mate; beards just visualise age.
Histogram of ages at death, normalized to fraction then to per-1000 individuals.
Build survivorship curve by stacking the same bars; the name cumulative distribution given after.
Reading the curve: safe at first, dangerous when energy runs out, then steady; parental memory explanation.
Second graph: death chance given survival to that age (8 of 217 = 3.7%, not 0.8%); retire the old graph.
Constant hazard means no aging; senescence defined versus aging.
Aging gene with 20 alleles, each encoding death at a set age.
Predict and write down; hindsight-bias warning.
Early death alleles go extinct; extrinsic vs intrinsic mortality named.
Main idea: selection weakens with age because something else may kill you first; insects vs tortoises.
Run to end: no-aging allele wins, so model fails to reproduce real life.
Add mutation: normal vs mutant death allele (30 s), 5% mutation, plus a do-nothing control gene.
Control sits at 50/50; mutant near 10%; pop quiz dominant or recessive.
Mutation accumulation named; still unrealistic (one gene).
10 copies of the gene, three-way prediction; no blob lives past 30 s; mutant alleles reinforce each other.
Selection weakened by internal mortality too; extreme settings admitted.
10,201 genes, realistic mutation rate 1e-5, multiplied-survival worked example; disclosed tuning.
3D graph of activation vs death chance vs frequency; predict.
Clarify two senses of mutation accumulation.
Some death alleles fix by luck; selection, mutation, drift forces; genetic drift and fixation named; misconception that every trait is adaptive.
Result is a ramp that looks like real aging.
Antagonistic pleiotropy: overdrive muscle allele doubles speed, 5% death per second; it takes over.
Early reproduction worth more than late; p53 real example.
Restate key concept and two mechanisms.

metrics.key_term: natural selection gets weaker with age (senescence)
metrics.misconception: yes: natural selection should remove aging; every trait has an adaptive explanation (25:41)
metrics.brute_force: yes 4:00: run no-aging sim, tally deaths by age, build curves by hand before any aging gene
metrics.examples: baseline, 20-allele gene, single mutant gene + control, 10 genes, 10,201 genes, pleiotropy; escalating realism
metrics.ending: Recap of one big concept and two mechanisms, resources, teleprompter joke

principles.2: confirmed: graph built stepwise; each name (cumulative distribution, senescence, intrinsic) only after the thing is seen; 'retire' old graph (8:14)
principles.3: confirmed: survivorship and hazard graphs reused across all later sims; destiny colours persist
principles.4: partly: insects vs tortoises is an intuition after the result, not an entry analogy
principles.5: confirmed: blobs eat mangoes, starve, mate; beards age on screen (3:11-4:00)
principles.6: confirmed: no-aging baseline first, then hand-built curves; 20-allele toy before realistic (4:00, 9:06)
principles.7: confirmed: predict prompts at 9:53, 17:39, 23:19; learner told to write predictions (10:09)
principles.8: partly: speech steady; idea rate slows by long sims and a 3-part prediction (18:12), but fast stretches ('continue with a bit more speed' 13:42) and dense definitions pile up near 24:05
principles.9: confirmed: same mutate-and-test frame 1 gene, 10 genes, 10,201 genes
principles.10: confirmed: 1 gene to 10 to 10,201; 100 blobs to realistic scale (17:39, 19:47)
principles.11: confirmed: failure of selection-only model motivates mutation, then mutation scale, then pleiotropy (14:21)
principles.12: confirmed: papers, p53, Medawar lecture, Ageless book, Loyal dog trial (28:57-31:40)
principles.13: partly: plain explanations plus expert terms (drift, fixation, pleiotropy) and a simple conceptual summary at 11:51; why-this-tool is explicit (control gene 15:43)

new_moves.name: do-nothing-control
new_moves.what: Add a no-effect gene as a baseline so learner can read the effect against drift

new_moves.name: retire-a-graph
new_moves.what: State explicitly that an earlier graph is replaced by a more informative one and why

new_moves.name: one-sentence-priority
new_moves.what: Tell the learner the single idea to remember if they remember one thing

new_moves.name: extreme-then-realistic
new_moves.what: Show an exaggerated version to expose the effect, admit it is unconvincing, then rebuild realistically

new_moves.name: parameter-tuning-disclosure
new_moves.what: Say you tried numbers until something worked and why too high or too low fails

theory: The video builds from a failing model: each sim shows aging disappearing, the failure names the next ingredient, and each ingredient is first tested in an exaggerated form with a control. Concept priority is explicit (selection weakens with age), and every later mechanism is shown as a consequence. Honesty about tuning and extremes buys trust.
velocity: Scene builder: support controls (do-nothing baseline) in every comparative sim.
Orchestrator: playbook 'extreme then realistic' with explicit admission of exaggeration.
Voice: state the one idea to keep before the details, and later restate.
Learner model: use inline-quiz with dominance question as an optional prerequisite probe.
Evals: confirm every graph is built from an earlier one or retired explicitly.
quote: natural selection gets weaker the longer a creature's been alive
